sanskrit: nārāyaṇagiriṃ te tu garjanto rākṣasāmbudāḥ avarṣann iṣuvarṣeṇa varṣeṇādrim ivāmbudāḥ
english: Those demon-clouds, roaring, rained down a shower of arrows upon the mountain that was Nārāyaṇa, as storm-clouds rain upon a mountain.

sanskrit: śyāmāvadātas tair viṣṇur nīlair naktaṃcarottamaiḥ vṛto 'ñjanagirīvāsīd varṣamāṇaiḥ payodharaiḥ
english: Viṣṇu, dark-complexioned, encircled by those dark-hued foremost night-wanderers as they poured down their shafts, stood like the Añjana mountain wreathed in rain-bearing clouds.

sanskrit: śalabhā iva kedāraṃ maśakā iva parvatam yathāmṛtaghaṭaṃ jīvā makarā iva cārṇavam
english: As locusts descend upon a field, as gnats upon a mountain, as souls upon a jar of nectar, as sea-monsters upon the ocean —

sanskrit: tathā rakṣodhanur muktā vajrānilamanojavāḥ hariṃ viśanti sma śarā lokāstam iva paryaye
english: — so did the arrows discharged from the bows of the rākṣasas, swift as lightning and wind, enter into Hari as the worlds enter into the sun at the end of an age.

sanskrit: syandanaiḥ syandanagatā gajaiś ca gajadhūr gatāḥ aśvārohāḥ sadaśvaiś ca pādātāś cāmbare carāḥ
english: Warriors mounted on chariots drove forward in chariots; those at the fronts of elephants came on elephants; cavalrymen on swift horses; and the foot-soldiers moved through the air.

sanskrit: rākṣasendrā girinibhāḥ śaraśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ nirucchvāsaṃ hariṃ cakruḥ prāṇāyāma iva dvijam
english: The rākṣasa lords, mountain-like in size, assailed Hari with arrows, śaktis, ṛṣṭis, and tomaras, leaving him breathless, as breath-control exercises leave a twice-born man breathless.

sanskrit: niśācarais tudyamāno mīnair iva mahātimiḥ śārṅgam āyamya gātrāṇi rākṣasānāṃ mahāhave
english: Tormented by the night-wanderers as a great sea-monster is tormented by fish, he drew the Śārṅga bow and aimed at the bodies of the rākṣasas in that great battle.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair vajravaktrair manojavaiḥ ciccheda tilaśo viṣṇuḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: With arrows fully drawn and released, bearing tips like thunderbolts and swift as thought, Viṣṇu cut them to pieces, by the hundred, by the thousand.

sanskrit: vidrāvya śaravarṣaṃ taṃ varṣaṃ vāyur ivotthitam pāñcajanyaṃ mahāśaṅkhaṃ pradadhmau puruṣottamaḥ
english: Having dispersed that shower of arrows as the wind disperses a rain-cloud, the Puruṣottama blew his great conch Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: so 'mbujo hariṇā dhmātaḥ sarvaprāṇena śaṅkharāṭ rarāsa bhīmanihrādo yugānte jalado yathā
english: That lotus-born conch-king, blown by Hari with full breath, resounded with a terrifying roar like a thundercloud at the end of an age.

sanskrit: śaṅkharājaravaḥ so 'tha trāsayām āsa rākṣasān mṛgarāja ivāraṇye samadān iva kuñjarān
english: That sound of the conch-king then struck terror into the rākṣasas as a lion in the forest terrifies rutting elephants.

sanskrit: na śekur aśvāḥ saṃsthātuṃ vimadāḥ kuñjarābhavan syandanebhyaś cyutā yodhāḥ śaṅkharāvitadurbalāḥ
english: The horses could not stand still; the elephants lost their rut; warriors fell from their chariots, debilitated by the overwhelming sound of the conch.

sanskrit: śārṅgacāpavinirmuktā vajratulyānanāḥ śarāḥ vidārya tāni rakṣāṃsi supuṅkhā viviśuḥ kṣitim
english: The arrows discharged from the Śārṅga bow, their faces like thunderbolts, well-feathered, tore through those rākṣasas and buried themselves in the earth.

sanskrit: bhidyamānāḥ śaraiś cānye nārāyaṇadhanuścyutaiḥ nipetū rākṣasā bhīmāḥ śailā vajrahatā iva
english: Others, the fearsome rākṣasas, split asunder by the arrows released from Nārāyaṇa's bow, fell like mountains struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: vraṇair vraṇakarārīṇām adhokṣajaśarodbhavaiḥ asṛk kṣaranti dhārābhiḥ svarṇadhārām ivācalāḥ
english: With wounds made by the arrows of Adhokṣaja the wound-causer, they streamed blood in rivulets like mountains streaming golden veins of ore.

sanskrit: śaṅkharājaravaś cāpi śārṅgacāparavas tathā rākṣasānāṃ ravāṃś cāpi grasate vaiṣṇavo ravaḥ
english: The sound of the conch-king, and the twang of the Śārṅga bow, and even the clamour of the rākṣasas — all were swallowed by the Vaiṣṇava roar.

sanskrit: sūryād iva karā ghorā ūrmayaḥ sāgarād iva parvatād iva nāgendrā vāryoghā iva cāmbudāt
english: As terrible rays stream from the sun, as waves from the ocean, as torrents of serpent-lords from a mountain, as floods of water from a rain-cloud —

sanskrit: tathā bāṇā vinirmuktāḥ śārṅgān narāyaṇeritāḥ nirdhāvantīṣavas tūrṇaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: — so did the arrows loosed from the Śārṅga and sped by Nārāyaṇa stream forth swiftly, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: śarabheṇa yathā siṃhāḥ siṃhena dviradā yathā dviradena yathā vyāghrā vyāghreṇa dvīpino yathā
english: As lions flee before a śarabha, as elephants before a lion, as tigers before an elephant, as leopards before a tiger —

sanskrit: dvīpinā ca yathā śvānaḥ śunā mārjārakā yathā mārjāreṇa yathā sarpāḥ sarpeṇa ca yathākhavaḥ
english: — as dogs before a leopard, as cats before a dog, as serpents before a cat, as mice before a serpent —

sanskrit: tathā te rākṣasā yuddhe viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā dravanti drāvitāś caiva śāyitāś ca mahītale
english: — so did those rākṣasas in battle flee before Viṣṇu the all-powerful, routed and laid low upon the earth.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ sahasrāṇi nihatya madhusūdanaḥ vārijaṃ nādayām āsa toyadaṃ surarāḍ iva
english: Having slain thousands of rākṣasas, Madhusūdana sounded his lotus-born conch like the king of gods sounds a thundercloud.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaśaragrastaṃ śaṅkhanādasuvihvalam yayau laṅkām abhimukhaṃ prabhagnaṃ rākṣasaṃ balam
english: The rākṣasa army, struck by Nārāyaṇa's arrows and utterly bewildered by the conch's blast, fled in utter rout toward Laṅkā.

sanskrit: prabhagne rākṣasabale nārāyaṇaśarāhate sumālī śaravarṣeṇa āvavāra raṇe harim
english: When the rākṣasa force was thus routed and struck down by Nārāyaṇa's arrows, Sumālin checked Hari in battle with a rain of shafts.

sanskrit: utkṣipya hemābharaṇaṃ karaṃ karam iva dvipaḥ rarāsa rākṣaso harṣāt sataḍit toyado yathā
english: Raising his gold-ornamented arm like an elephant raising its trunk, the rākṣasa roared with joy like a thundercloud with lightning.

sanskrit: sumāler nardatas tasya śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam ciccheda yantur aśvāś ca bhrāntās tasya tu rakṣasaḥ
english: Even as Sumālin was roaring thus, Hari severed his head with its blazing earrings, and the rākṣasa's charioteer and his horses were thrown into confusion.

sanskrit: tair aśvair bhrāmyate bhrāntaiḥ sumālī rākṣaseśvaraḥ indriyāśvair yathā bhrāntair dhṛtihīno yathā naraḥ
english: Sumālin, lord of rākṣasas, was whirled about by those bewildered horses as a man without self-control is whirled about by his bewildered senses.

sanskrit: mālī cābhyadravad yuddhe pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ māler dhanuścyutā bāṇāḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitāḥ viviśur harim āsādya krauñcaṃ patrarathā iva
english: Mālin also rushed forward in battle, seizing his arrow-fitted bow; the arrows decorated with gold that flew from Mālin's bow reached Hari and entered him as birds enter the Krauñca mountain.

sanskrit: ardyamānaḥ śaraiḥ so 'tha mālimuktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ cukṣubhe na raṇe viṣṇur jitendriya ivādhibhiḥ
english: Though tormented by thousands of arrows released by Mālin, Viṣṇu did not waver in battle, as a man of conquered senses is not shaken by afflictions.

sanskrit: atha maurvī svanaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ mālinaṃ prati bāṇaughān sasarjāsigadādharaḥ
english: Then the Bhagavān, the nurturer of all beings, wielder of sword and mace, twanged his bowstring and let loose floods of arrows upon Mālin.

sanskrit: te mālideham āsādya vajravidyutprabhāḥ śarāḥ pibanti rudhiraṃ tasya nāgā iva purāmṛtam
english: Those arrows, gleaming like thunderbolts and lightning, reached Mālin's body and drank his blood as serpents of old drank nectar.

sanskrit: mālinaṃ vimukhaṃ kṛtvā mālimauliṃ harir balāt rathaṃ ca sadhvajaṃ cāpaṃ vājinaś ca nyapātayat
english: Having turned Mālin to flight, Hari forcibly struck down Mālin's crest, his chariot with its banner, his bow, and his horses.

sanskrit: virathas tu gadāṃ gṛhya mālī naktaṃcarottamaḥ āpupluve gadāpāṇir giryagrād iva keṣarī
english: The foremost night-wanderer Mālin, deprived of his chariot, seized his mace and leapt forward, mace in hand, like a lion leaping from a mountain peak.

sanskrit: sa tayā garuḍaṃ saṃkhye īśānam iva cāntakaḥ lalāṭadeśe 'bhyahanad vajreṇendro yathācalam
english: With that mace he struck Garuḍa on the forehead in battle as Death strikes Śiva, as Indra strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt.

sanskrit: gadayābhihatas tena mālinā garuḍo bhṛśam raṇāt parāṅmukhaṃ devaṃ kṛtavān vedanāturaḥ
english: Garuḍa, sorely struck by Mālin's mace, turned the god away from the battle, overwhelmed by pain.

sanskrit: parāṅmukhe kṛte deve mālinā garuḍena vai udatiṣṭhan mahānādo rakṣasām abhinardatām
english: When the god was turned away by Mālin and Garuḍa, a great tumultuous shout arose from the exulting rākṣasas.

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ nadatāṃ nādaṃ śrutvā harihayānujaḥ parāṅmukho 'py utsasarja cakraṃ mālijighāṃsayā
english: Hearing the clamour of the roaring rākṣasas, the younger brother of Indra's steed — even as he turned away — let fly his discus with the intent to slay Mālin.

sanskrit: tat sūryamaṇḍalābhāsaṃ svabhāsā bhāsayan nabhaḥ kālacakranibhaṃ cakraṃ māleḥ śīrṣam apātayat
english: That discus, blazing like the solar orb, illuminating the sky with its own radiance, resembling the wheel of Time, severed Mālin's head.

sanskrit: tacchiro rākṣasendrasya cakrotkṛttaṃ vibhīṣaṇam papāta rudhirodgāri purā rāhuśiro yathā
english: The severed, horrifying head of that rākṣasa lord, cut off by the discus, spouting blood, fell as Rāhu's head fell of old.

sanskrit: tataḥ suraiḥ susaṃhṛṣṭaiḥ sarvaprāṇasamīritaḥ siṃhanādaravo muktaḥ sādhu deveti vādibhiḥ
english: Then the gods, greatly rejoiced, uttered with full voice a lion's roar of triumph, crying "Excellent! Excellent, O god!"

sanskrit: mālinaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā sumālī malyavān api sabalau śokasaṃtaptau laṅkāṃ prati vidhāvitau
english: Seeing Mālin slain, Sumālin and Mālyavān too, both tormented by grief, fled together with their forces toward Laṅkā.

sanskrit: garuḍas tu samāśvastaḥ saṃnivṛtya mahāmanāḥ rākṣasān drāvayām āsa pakṣavātena kopitaḥ
english: Garuḍa, great-souled, recovering himself, wheeled back and, enraged, scattered the rākṣasas with the gale of his wings.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇo 'pīṣuvarāśanībhir vidārayām āsa dhanuḥpramuktaiḥ naktaṃcarān muktavidhūtakeśān yathāśanībhiḥ sataḍinmahendraḥ
english: Nārāyaṇa too tore apart the night-wanderers with arrow-thunderbolts released from his bow — their hair dishevelled as they fled — as the great Indra tears apart with his lightning-laden thunderbolts.

sanskrit: bhinnātapatraṃ patamānaśastraṃ śarair apadhvastaviśīrṇadeham viniḥsṛtāntraṃ bhayalolanetraṃ balaṃ tad unmattanibhaṃ babhūva
english: With parasols shattered, weapons falling, bodies rent and mangled by arrows, entrails streaming out, eyes rolling in terror, that army resembled a host of madmen.

sanskrit: siṃhārditānām iva kuñjarāṇāṃ niśācarāṇāṃ saha kuñjarāṇām ravāś ca vegāś ca samaṃ babhūvuḥ purāṇasiṃhena vimarditānām
english: The cries and the speeds of those night-wanderers together with their elephants were like those of elephants crushed by the ancient lion, tormented by a lion.

sanskrit: saṃchādyamānā haribāṇajālaiḥ svabāṇajālāni samutsṛjantaḥ dhāvanti naktaṃcarakālameghā vāyupraṇunnā iva kālameghāḥ
english: Covered over by Hari's net of arrows yet discharging their own nets of arrows, the dark-cloud-like night-wanderers fled as dark clouds driven by the wind.

sanskrit: cakraprahārair vinikṛttaśīrṣāḥ saṃcūrṇitāṅgāś ca gadāprahāraiḥ asiprahārair bahudhā vibhaktāḥ patanti śailā iva rākṣasendrāḥ
english: Their heads severed by blows of the discus, their limbs crushed by mace-blows, their bodies split apart in many ways by sword-blows, the rākṣasa lords fell like mountains.

sanskrit: cakrakṛttāsyakamalā gadāsaṃcūrṇitorasaḥ lāṅgalaglapitagrīvā musalair bhinnamastakāḥ
english: Their lotus-faces cut off by the discus, their chests pounded to pieces by the mace, their necks wrung by the plough-weapon, their skulls shattered by the pestle —

sanskrit: ke cic caivāsinā chinnās tathānye śaratāḍitāḥ nipetur ambarāt tūrṇaṃ rākṣasāḥ sāgarāmbhasi
english: — and some cut down by the sword, others struck by arrows, the rākṣasas fell swiftly from the sky into the waters of the ocean.

sanskrit: tadāmbaraṃ vigalitahārakuṇḍalair niśācarair nīlabalāhakopamaiḥ nipātyamānair dadṛśe nirantaraṃ nipātyamānair iva nīlaparvataiḥ
english: The sky at that time, with night-wanderers resembling dark storm-clouds falling continuously — their garlands and earrings streaming loose — appeared as though blue mountains were falling without cease.

sanskrit: hanyamāne bale tasmin padmanābhena pṛṣṭhataḥ mālyavān saṃnivṛtto 'tha velātiga ivārṇavaḥ
english: While that army was being slaughtered from behind by Padmanābha, Mālyavān turned back like an ocean overflowing its shore.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayanaḥ kopāc calan maulir niśācaraḥ padmanābham idaṃ prāha vacanaṃ paruṣaṃ tadā
english: With eyes reddened with rage, his crest quivering, the night-wanderer then spoke these harsh words to Padmanābha:

sanskrit: nārāyaṇa na jānīṣe kṣatradharmaṃ sanātanam ayuddhamanaso bhagnān yo 'smān haṃsi yathetaraḥ
english: "O Nārāyaṇa, you do not know the eternal code of the warrior — you who slay us, who have no will to fight and are already broken, as if we were ordinary foes.

sanskrit: parāṅmukhavadhaṃ pāpaṃ yaḥ karoti sureśvara sa hantā na gataḥ svargaṃ labhate puṇyakarmaṇām
english: O lord of gods, the slayer who kills those turned in flight commits a sin; such a killer does not attain the heaven won by those of righteous deeds.

sanskrit: yuddhaśraddhātha vā te 'sti śaṅkhacakragadādhara ahaṃ sthito 'smi paśyāmi balaṃ darśaya yat tava
english: Or if you have any relish for battle, O bearer of conch, discus, and mace, I stand before you — I am watching. Show whatever strength is yours."

sanskrit: uvāca rākṣasendraṃ taṃ devarājānujo balī yuṣmatto bhayabhītānāṃ devānāṃ vai mayābhayam rākṣasotsādanaṃ dattaṃ tad etad anupālyate
english: The mighty younger brother of the king of gods answered that lord of rākṣasas: "I have pledged freedom from fear to the gods who are terror-stricken because of you; the extermination of the rākṣasas is the pledge I am upholding.

sanskrit: prāṇair api priyaṃ kāryaṃ devānāṃ hi sadā mayā so 'haṃ vo nihaniṣyāmi rasātalagatān api
english: The welfare of the gods is ever dearer to me than my own life. I shall slay you even if you have gone down to the netherworld."

sanskrit: devam evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu raktāmburuhalocanam śaktyā bibheda saṃkruddho rākṣasendro rarāsa ca
english: As the god was speaking thus — his eyes red as blood-red lotuses — the infuriated rākṣasa lord pierced him with a śakti weapon and roared.

sanskrit: mālyavad bhujanirmuktā śaktir ghaṇṭākṛtasvanā harer urasi babhrāja meghastheva śatahradā
english: The śakti released from Mālyavān's arm, sounding like a bell, blazed upon Hari's chest like a hundred-streaked lightning bolt within a cloud.

sanskrit: tatas tām eva cotkṛṣya śaktiṃ śaktidharapriyaḥ mālyavantaṃ samuddiśya cikṣepāmburuhekṣaṇaḥ
english: Then the lotus-eyed god, beloved of Śakti's bearer Skanda, pulled out that very śakti and hurled it back at Mālyavān.

sanskrit: skandotsṛṣṭeva sā śaktir govindakaraniḥsṛtā kāṅkṣantī rākṣasaṃ prāyān maholkevāñjanācalam
english: That śakti, released from Govinda's hand as if hurled by Skanda himself, sped toward the rākṣasa like a great meteor toward the Añjana mountain.

sanskrit: sā tasyorasi vistīrṇe hārabhāsāvabhāsite apatad rākṣasendrasya girikūṭa ivāśaniḥ
english: It fell upon the broad chest of the rākṣasa lord, gleaming with the radiance of his necklaces, like a thunderbolt upon a mountain peak.

sanskrit: tayā bhinnatanutrāṇāḥ prāviśad vipulaṃ tamaḥ mālyavān punar āśvastas tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: His armour pierced by it, he entered into vast darkness; but Mālyavān recovered himself and stood immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ kārṣṇāyasaṃ śūlaṃ kaṇṭakair bahubhiś citam pragṛhyābhyahanad devaṃ stanayor antare dṛḍham
english: Then seizing a black-iron trident studded with many spikes, he struck the god firmly between the breasts.

sanskrit: tathaiva raṇaraktas tu muṣṭinā vāsavānujam tāḍayitvā dhanurmātram apakrānto niśācaraḥ
english: Flushed with battle-lust, he further struck the younger brother of Vāsava with his fist and then retreated a bowshot's distance.

sanskrit: tato 'mbare mahāñ śabdaḥ sādhu sādhv iti cotthitaḥ āhatya rākṣaso viṣṇuṃ garuḍaṃ cāpy atāḍayat
english: Then a great cry arose in the sky: "Excellent! Excellent!" — for the rākṣasa had struck both Viṣṇu and Garuḍa.

sanskrit: vainateyas tataḥ kruddhaḥ pakṣavātena rākṣasaṃ vyapohad balavān vāyuḥ śuṣkaparṇacayam yathā
english: Then the son of Vinatā, Garuḍa, enraged, swept the rākṣasa away with the gale of his wings as a powerful wind sweeps away a heap of dry leaves.

sanskrit: dvijendrapakṣavātena drāvitaṃ dṛśya pūrvajam sumālī svabalaiḥ sārdhaṃ laṅkām abhimukho yayau
english: Seeing his elder brother routed by the wing-wind of the king of birds, Sumālin turned toward Laṅkā together with his own forces.

sanskrit: pakṣavātabaloddhūto mālyavān api rākṣasaḥ svabalena samāgamya yayau laṅkāṃ hriyā vṛtaḥ
english: Mālyavān the rākṣasa, blown aloft by the force of the wing-wind, gathered his forces and also went to Laṅkā, wrapped in shame.

sanskrit: evaṃ te rākṣasā rāma hariṇā kamalekṣaṇa bahuśaḥ saṃyuge bhagnā hatapravaranāyakāḥ
english: Thus, O Rāma, those rākṣasas were many times routed in battle by Hari of the lotus eyes, their foremost commanders slain.

sanskrit: aśaknuvantas te viṣṇuṃ pratiyoddhuṃ bhayārditāḥ tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatā vastuṃ pātālaṃ sahapatnayaḥ
english: Unable to withstand Viṣṇu, tormented by fear, they abandoned Laṅkā and went to dwell in Pātāla together with their wives.

sanskrit: sumālinaṃ samāsādya rākṣasaṃ raghunandana sthitāḥ prakhyātavīryās te vaṃśe sālakaṭaṅkaṭe
english: Those renowned for their valour, O joy of the Raghu line, took refuge with the rākṣasa Sumālin and remained in the lineage of Sālakaṭaṅkaṭa.

sanskrit: ye tvayā nihatās te vai paulastyā nāma rākṣasāḥ sumālī mālyavān mālī ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ sarva ete mahābhāga rāvaṇād balavattarāḥ
english: Those rākṣasas called Paulastyas whom you slew — Sumālin, Mālyavān, Mālin, and those who were their forerunners — all of them, O illustrious one, were mightier than Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: na cānyo rakṣasāṃ hantā sureṣv api puraṃjaya ṛte nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam
english: There is no other slayer of those rākṣasas, even among the gods, O conqueror of citadels, save the god Nārāyaṇa, bearer of conch, discus, and mace.

sanskrit: bhavān nārāyaṇo devaś caturbāhuḥ sanātanaḥ rākṣasān hantum utpanno ajeyaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ
english: You yourself are the god Nārāyaṇa, four-armed, eternal — born to slay the rākṣasas, unconquerable, the imperishable Lord.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya sumālī nāma rākṣasaḥ rasātalān martyalokaṃ sarvaṃ vai vicacāra ha
english: Then, after some time, the rākṣasa named Sumālin wandered all through the mortal world, having come up from Rasātala.

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśas taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ kanyāṃ duhitaraṃ gṛhya vinā padmam iva śriyam athāpaśyat sa gacchantaṃ puṣpakeṇa dhaneśvaram
english: Dark as a blue thundercloud, with earrings of refined gold, he was taking his daughter — like Śrī without her lotus — when he caught sight of the lord of wealth travelling in the Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvāmarasaṃkāśaṃ gacchantaṃ pāvakopamam athābbravīt sutāṃ rakṣaḥ kaikasīṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: Seeing him pass by, resplendent as an immortal, blazing like fire, the rākṣasa then spoke to his daughter Kaikasī by name:

sanskrit: putri pradānakālo 'yaṃ yauvanaṃ te 'tivartate tvatkṛte ca vayaṃ sarve yantritā dharmabuddhayaḥ
english: "Daughter, the time for your bestowal has come; your youth is passing. For your sake we are all restrained, dharma-minded in our thoughts.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sapadmeva putrike pratyākhyānāc ca bhītais tvaṃ na varaiḥ pratigṛhyase
english: You, my dear, are endowed with every virtue, like Śrī with her lotus; yet through fear of rejection you have not been accepted by suitors.

sanskrit: kanyāpitṛtvaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ mānakāṅkṣiṇām na jñāyate ca kaḥ kanyāṃ varayed iti putrike
english: The lot of a girl's father is indeed difficult for all who seek honour; for one never knows, my daughter, who will seek a maiden's hand.

sanskrit: mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulaṃ yatra caiva pradīyate kulatrayaṃ sadā kanyā saṃśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati
english: A maiden always places in uncertainty these three lineages: her mother's line, her father's line, and the line into which she is given.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ munivaraśreṣṭhaṃ prajāpatikulodbhavam gaccha viśravasaṃ putri paulastyaṃ varaya svayam
english: Therefore go, my daughter, and choose for yourself Viśravas, the foremost of the best of sages, born of the Prajāpati lineage, of the Paulastya family.

sanskrit: īdṛśās te bhaviṣyanti putrāḥ putri na saṃśayaḥ tejasā bhāskarasamā yādṛśo 'yaṃ dhaneśvaraḥ
english: Sons such as that lord of wealth — equal to the sun in splendour — will be yours without doubt, my daughter."

sanskrit: etasminn antare rāma pulastyatanayo dvijaḥ agnihotram upātiṣṭhac caturtha iva pāvakaḥ
english: At that very moment, O Rāma, the twice-born son of Pulastya — Viśravas — was tending his sacred fire, blazing like a fourth flame.

sanskrit: sā tu tāṃ dāruṇāṃ velām acintya pitṛgauravāt upasṛtyāgratas tasya caraṇādhomukhī sthitā
english: Without considering the inauspicious hour, out of reverence for her father, she approached him and stood before him with her face downcast at his feet.

sanskrit: sa tu tāṃ vīkṣya suśroṇīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām abravīt paramodāro dīpyamāna ivaujasā
english: He, blazing with splendour, most magnanimous, looked at her — her face like the full moon, her hips lovely — and spoke:

sanskrit: bhadre kasyāsi duhitā kuto vā tvam ihāgatā kiṃ kāryaṃ kasya vā hetos tattvato brūhi śobhane
english: "Auspicious one, whose daughter are you? Whence have you come here? What is your purpose, and for what reason? Tell me truly, O radiant one."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā kanyā kṛtāñjalir athābravīt ātmaprabhāvena mune jñātum arhasi me matam
english: Thus addressed, the maiden joined her palms and said: "By your own power, O sage, you are able to know my intention.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu viddhi hi māṃ brahmañ śāsanāt pitur āgatām kaikasī nāma nāmnāhaṃ śeṣaṃ tvaṃ jñātum arhasi
english: Yet know this, O brahman: I have come by my father's command. I am named Kaikasī — the rest you are worthy to divine."

sanskrit: sa tu gatvā munir dhyānaṃ vākyam etad uvāca ha vijñātaṃ te mayā bhadre kāraṇaṃ yan manogatam
english: The sage entered into meditation and then spoke these words: "I have understood, O auspicious one, the purpose that is in your heart.

sanskrit: dāruṇāyāṃ tu velāyāṃ yasmāt tvaṃ mām upasthitā śṛṇu tasmāt sutān bhadre yādṛśāñ janayiṣyasi
english: But because you have come to me at a dreadful hour, hear, O auspicious one, what manner of sons you shall beget.

sanskrit: dāruṇān dāruṇākārān dāruṇābhijanapriyān prasaviṣyasi suśroṇi rākṣasān krūrakarmaṇaḥ
english: You shall bear, O fair-hipped one, rākṣasas who are fierce, fierce in form, beloved of the fierce — cruel in their deeds."

sanskrit: sā tu tad vacanaṃ śrutvā praṇipatyābravīd vacaḥ bhagavan nedṛśāḥ putrās tvatto 'rhā brahmayonitaḥ
english: Hearing those words she prostrated herself and said: "O Bhagavān, sons such as these are not fitting from you who are born of Brahmā's line."

sanskrit: athābravīn munis tatra paścimo yas tavātmajaḥ mama vaṃśānurūpaś ca dharmātmā ca bhaviṣyati
english: Then the sage said: "The last-born of your sons shall be in keeping with my lineage and shall be righteous in spirit."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā kanyā rāma kālena kena cit janayām āsa bībhatsaṃ rakṣorūpaṃ sudāruṇam
english: Thus spoken to, that maiden, O Rāma, after some time brought forth a hideous, most fearsome form of a rākṣasa.

sanskrit: daśaśīrṣaṃ mahādaṃṣṭraṃ nīlāñjanacayopamam tāmrauṣṭhaṃ viṃśatibhujaṃ mahāsyaṃ dīptamūrdhajam
english: Ten-headed, great-fanged, resembling a heap of dark collyrium, copper-lipped, twenty-armed, vast-mouthed, with blazing hair —

sanskrit: jātamātre tatas tasmin sajvālakavalāḥ śivāḥ kravyādāś cāpasavyāni maṇḍalāni pracakrire
english: The moment he was born, jackals with blazing mouths and carnivorous birds began circling in the inauspicious direction.

sanskrit: vavarṣa rudhiraṃ devo meghāś ca kharanisvanāḥ prababhau na ca khe sūryo maholkāś cāpatan bhuvi
english: The sky rained blood; the clouds brayed harshly; the sun did not shine in the sky; great meteors fell upon the earth.

sanskrit: atha nāmākarot tasya pitāmahasamaḥ pitā daśaśīrṣaḥ prasūto 'yaṃ daśagrīvo bhaviṣyati
english: Then his father, equal to the Grandfather Brahmā, gave him his name: "Born ten-headed, this one shall be Daśagrīva — the ten-necked."

sanskrit: tasya tv anantaraṃ jātaḥ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ pramāṇād yasya vipulaṃ pramāṇaṃ neha vidyate
english: After him was born Kumbhakarṇa, of immense strength — his measure is not found anywhere in this world.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā nāma saṃjajñe vikṛtānanā vibhīṣaṇaś ca dharmātmā kaikasyāḥ paścimaḥ sutaḥ
english: Then was born one named Śūrpaṇakhā, of hideous face; and Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, was the last son of Kaikasī.

sanskrit: te tu tatra mahāraṇye vavṛdhuḥ sumahaujasaḥ teṣāṃ krūro daśagrīvo lokodvegakaro 'bhavat
english: They grew up there in the great forest, endowed with immense energy. Among them Daśagrīva was fierce, a cause of terror to the worlds.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaḥ pramattas tu maharṣīn dharmasaṃśritān trailokyaṃ trāsayan duṣṭo bhakṣayan vicacāra ha
english: Kumbhakarṇa, reckless and depraved, wandered about devouring the great sages who were given to dharma, terrorising the three worlds.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā nityaṃ dharmapathe sthitaḥ svādhyāyaniyatāhāra uvāsa niyatendriyaḥ
english: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, was ever established on the path of dharma — devoted to study, regulated in his diet, with his senses restrained.

sanskrit: atha vitteśvaro devas tatra kālena kena cit āgacchat pitaraṃ draṣṭuṃ puṣpakeṇa mahaujasaṃ
english: Then, after some time, the god Vitteśvara — the lord of wealth — came there in his Puṣpaka chariot, of great splendour, to visit his father.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikasī tatra jvalantam iva tejasā āsthāya rākṣasīṃ buddhiṃ daśagrīvam uvāca ha
english: Seeing him blazing with splendour, Kaikasī there took on a rākṣasa mind and spoke to Daśagrīva:

sanskrit: putravaiśravaṇaṃ paśya bhrātaraṃ tejasā vṛtam bhrātṛbhāve same cāpi paśyātmānaṃ tvam īdṛśam
english: "My son, see Vaiśravaṇa, your brother, invested with splendour — and though you stand equal to him as a brother, see what you yourself are.

sanskrit: daśagrīva tathā yatnaṃ kuruṣvāmitavikrama yathā bhavasi me putra śīghraṃ vaiśvaraṇopamaḥ
english: O Daśagrīva, O you of immeasurable valour, make such effort so that you, my son, may quickly become the equal of Vaiśravaṇa."

sanskrit: mātus tad vacanaṃ śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān amarṣam atulaṃ lebhe pratijñāṃ cākarot tadā
english: Hearing his mother's words, the illustrious Daśagrīva was seized by unequalled indignation and made a vow:

sanskrit: satyaṃ te pratijānāmi tulyo bhrātrādhiko 'pi vā bhaviṣyāmy acirān mātaḥ saṃtāpaṃ tyaja hṛdgatam
english: "I promise you truly: I shall soon become the equal of my brother — or even his superior. Mother, cast away the sorrow in your heart."

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhena tenaiva daśagrīvaḥ sahānujaḥ prāpsyāmi tapasā kāmam iti kṛtvādhyavasya ca āgacchad ātmasiddhyarthaṃ gokarṇasyāśramaṃ śubham
english: Then, impelled by that very wrath, Daśagrīva together with his younger brothers, having resolved "I shall attain my desire through austerity," came to the auspicious hermitage of Gokarṇa for the accomplishment of his purpose.
